title.narrative: Early Action For Impact (EAFI)- LDS START READY

description.narrative: The main objective of the anticipatory action project is to enhance community resilience in four wards of Gwanda (17, 18, 19, and 20) by proactively addressing the anticipated crises related to food, water, and livestock due to the ongoing drought. This initiative focuses on implementing strategies that mitigate the adverse impacts of climate variability, particularly the El Niño phenomenon, while supporting vulnerable populations in adapting to these changing conditions. The project aims to directly reach 5859 vulnerable households, with a target demographic of 60% female and 40% male participants. Additionally, the project is expected to inform an estimated 60,000 listeners through the Manama local radio station as part of its early warning system efforts, enhancing community awareness and preparedness. The project seeks to conduct water yield capacity testing for existing boreholes, mechanise them with solar energy to allow water to be accessed and distributed to villages for household use and their livestock watering. Mechanisation of boreholes will cut on chore drudgery especially for women and girls who bear burden of long distance to collect water due to gendered distribution of housework. Mechanical harvesting of water will enable both humans and livestock to have adequate water for survival during and post the emergency. The project also seeks to provide pasture and crop starter packs which will allow preservation of livestock and improve food security of the vulnerable households. Provision of acaricides and fodder will enhance asset protection (livestock) through averting livestock poverty losses. Training on agronomical practices using Training of Trainer (ToT) model will promote cascading, peer learning local level knowledge generation to avert future drought induced crises. The project seeks to support coordination efforts of both government and local structures. Coordination is key during such times as this when the communities are in desperate need for support.
